Hey Tim - thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on technical requirements before the SE deep-dive.

Summary of what I heard from your team:
- Desired TTFT (time-to-first-token) target: <= 250ms p95 for single-request streaming responses (multi-turn chat).
- Sustained throughput: ~800 requests/minute during peak windows; expected burst to ~2.5k rpm for short periods.
- Concurrency: ~120 concurrent active connections (mostly streaming).
- Streaming transport: prefer Server-Sent Events (SSE) for browser clients, but WebSocket support is required for mobile SDKs.
- Chunk cadence: need low-latency incremental updates - ideally chunk cadence of ~100-200ms for UI responsiveness; ability to coalesce small tokens into ~50-200-byte chunks if helpful.

Open questions / asks from Redwood so we can size and scope the bench: 
1) Can you confirm whether the 250ms p95 TTFT is for 95th percentile across all requests or just for the 95th percentile during peak?
2) Are the requests CPU-bound (long prompts) or token-bound (very long outputs)? Any sample prompt examples you can share will help.
3) Do you need guaranteed ordering across chunked updates (yes/no)?
4) Will you accept short gaps between chunks during bursts (e.g., occasional 300-400ms) if overall TTFT SLO holds?

Next steps I propose:
- Share Keystone SLO template (attached) and a short mutual action plan (attached) with timeframe for SE deep-dive.
- Logan (SE) to do a tech feasibility note and recommend whether SSE/WebSocket or a hybrid is best for your UX.
- Schedule a 60-min SE deep-dive next week to align on load testing profile and perf targets.

If you can reply with answers to the questions above and a couple sample prompts (copy/paste), we can pre-size a test run and bring quantized model recommendations.

Thanks - talk soon,

2) Prompt mix: mostly short prompts (10-60 tokens) with medium outputs (avg 80-150 tokens). A small subset of requests will be long-form generation (~500-800 tokens) but only ~3% of traffic. I'll attach a few sanitized sample prompts separately.

Hi Tim / Marissa - short technical note from the SE side before the deep-dive.

TL;DR: Redwood can meet a 250ms p95 TTFT for the profile you described with the following implementation notes. We fully support both SSE and WebSocket streaming.

Key recommendations:
- Transport: Use SSE for web clients (simpler reconnect + HTTP/2 friendly) and WebSocket for mobile if your mobile SDK needs low reconnect latency. Redwood's runtime exposes identical chunk semantics over both transports.
- First-token latency: Ensure client connections are warmed (keep-alive) and avoid cold-starting model containers for in-band requests. For strict TTFT guarantees we recommend a small pre-warmed pool for peak windows.
- Chunk cadence: We recommend targeting 100-200ms chunk cadence for the majority of responses. For very short responses (<= 30 tokens) it's often better to send a single chunk to avoid overhead. For long responses, coalesce tokens into ~100-300 byte chunks to reduce network overhead while keeping UI responsiveness.
- Ordering: Redwood guarantees token order per-stream; clients must apply chunks in receipt order.
- Backpressure & concurrency: If you hit concurrency limits, Redwood can gracefully degrade by switching to a lower-capacity model variant or reducing chunk frequency. We'll include fallback policy options in the deep-dive.

Pre-deep-dive asks (to prepare a scoped load test):
- Example prompts (you said you'd share) + distribution (percent short/medium/long).
- Target sustained throughput and expected daily peak windows (timestamps/timezone).
- Any geographic constraints (region-specific latency).

I'll add a short tech agenda to the HubSpot deal and drop a link to Redwood's streaming best-practices doc here: https://docs.redwood.ai/streaming-best-practices

If 11/4 10:00 PT works for you Tim, let's lock it. I'll include a short load-test plan and SLO acceptance criteria in the calendar invite.
